text: 28h dense rows. At depth 5 the name gets 96px: 280 − 92 indent − 12 chevron − 12 icon − 4×8 gaps − 30 for the two toggles − 6 right pad. The long row here is the stress case. A row shows a custom name, else the element’s own first 32 characters, else the type label. Arrow keys move the selection, never focus — Down twice selects the same row twice, so the tree cannot be walked (LayerTreeItem.tsx:155-164). Every row is its own tab stop plus up to three more (:172). The eye and lock are 20px tall with no width set — about 15×20, under the 24×24 pointer minimum this 28h row can afford (layers-v2.css:157-178). The M/T breakpoint badges here can never render: buildTree returns five fields and never breakpointOverrides (useLayerTree.ts:88-95). Hidden and locked have no roll-up — the footer counts total and selected only, and search matches name, type, tag and id, not state (LayersTab.tsx:216-221, useLayerSearch.ts:16-24).

text: The line is drawn over illegal targets too — the drop is what refuses, not the hover. The reason appears as an alert at the top of the panel and clears itself after 3s. The reason is built from raw type ids — “button cannot contain children”, “text cannot be nested inside heading” — not the names on the rows, and a locked container refuses the drop with no locked-target affordance during the drag (index.tsx:87-93, 120-160).

Hidden is not deleted. 45% opacity, keeps its place in the tree. Dimming opens no undo step, so ⌘Z undoes your previous edit instead and the dim stays on — and it is stored in this browser only, so a collaborator does not see it. The glyph is an eye, the universal symbol for hide, on a control that hides nothing; the control that does is the Inspector’s Visibility section, and the two have no visible relationship (LayerTreeItem.tsx:285-306).

Locked has no row treatment: no dim, no tint. The only signals are the darker padlock, the aria-label suffix and draggable=false (LayerTreeItem.tsx:99, layers-v2.css has no locked rule). Lock is written to TWO places that never reconcile — a per-page localStorage set the panel re-reads, and ElementData.locked on the document, which is what the canvas enforces. hydrateFromStorage pushes storage INTO the engine and never reads element.isLocked() back, so on a second machine or after clearing site data the padlock draws OPEN while the canvas refuses the element and says “This element is locked. Unlock it in the Layers panel.” — naming the one control that is showing the opposite state (useLayerActions.ts:70-97,163-168; Element.ts:151-155; useSelectionBehavior.ts:88-95). And the lock only holds on one of the two surfaces: clicking this row selects the element normally and the Inspector edits it (useLayerSelection.ts:68-74).
